# In Review selection list poorly sorted

## Problem statement

The herdr TUI's In Review section displays work items with no audit (bucket 4 — "no audit yet") in the wrong priority order: medium-priority items appear before high-priority items. Low-priority items may also be misplaced.

## Users

- **Herdr users** (Pi plugin users managing work through the worklog system) — they rely on the In Review section to prioritise work items awaiting producer review. Seeing medium-priority items before high-priority items creates confusion and risks work on lower-priority items being done first.

### User story

As a herdr user viewing the In Review selection list, I expect high-priority items to appear before medium-priority items so I can triage the most important work first.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Items in the In Review section that are in the same audit bucket (particularly bucket 4 — no audit) are sorted with high priority first, then medium, then low.
2. The sorting applies consistently across all six audit buckets (needsProducerReview → failed-fresh → failed-stale → no-audit → passed-stale → passed-fresh).
3. Within the same bucket and same priority, items are ordered by updatedAt (older first) as the secondary sort key.
4. The fix works for both the default worklist (via `fetchNextItems` → `regroupWorkItems`) and the stage-filtered view (`/wl in_review` → `fetchItemsByStage` → `wl list` → `regroupWorkItems`).
5. All existing grouping and worklist tests continue to pass.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must maintain the existing six-bucket sort predicate and group assignment logic.
- Both `src/commands/grouping.ts` (CLI) and `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` (herdr plugin) must remain in sync.
- Must not change the group ordering (Critical Group N → Group N → Idea → Other → In Review).

## Existing state

The sorting logic for in_review items is defined in `compareInReviewItems` / `inReviewBucket` in both `src/commands/grouping.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`. Within the same bucket, items should sort by priority (high=0 → medium=1 → low=2), then updatedAt, then id as a tie-break.

The `wl list --stage in_review` command also sorts in_review items via `compareGroupableItems` (which delegates to `compareInReviewItems`), with a fallback to position-based ordering when buckets are equal.

## Desired change

Diagnose and fix the sorting discrepancy so that within-each-bucket priority ordering is correct (high → medium → low). This may require changes to `compareInReviewItems`, `compareGroupableItems`, or the `wl list` sorting logic in `src/commands/list.ts`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — `compareInReviewItems`, `compareGroupableItems`, `regroupWorkItems`
- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — CLI-side copy of the same functions (must stay in sync)
- `src/commands/list.ts` — `wl list --stage in_review` sorting path
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchNextItems`, `fetchItemsByStage` (fetch + regroup paths)
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — tests for in_review bucket sorting (ACL)

## Related work

- **Rewrite assignItemGroups + next.ts ordering** (WL-0MSAKPVR9005B6XJ) — established the within-group ordering spec including the 6-bucket in_review sort
- **Sort in_review items in the selection list by audit status** (WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV) — implemented bucket-based sorting in the selection list
- **Sort in_review items** (WL-0MSLPM5ZB003TADT) — original sorting specification for in_review items
- **Herdr plugin regroup fix** (WL-0MSAKPWIY005DL8W) — regroup logic for the worklist
- **audit reject should not change work item priority** (WL-0MUUAEDAU001GT1L) — related to priority handling in review workflow
- **Test: own-backlog fallback selection, scoping & fail-open** (WL-0MUZPBQQ3001DAM6) — selection logic tests

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** This is a sorting fix only. Do not modify group assignment, bucket thresholds, or the group display order.
- **Assumption:** The bug exists in the display/sorting layer, not in the data. The `wl list --json` output should be verified to confirm the sorting issue persists at the data layer.
- **Risk:** Changes to sorting may affect other parts of the worklist that depend on `compareGroupableItems`. Full test suite must pass.
- **Risk:** Both `src/commands/grouping.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` must be updated in lockstep — they are intentionally duplicated copies.

Implement `watchDbChanges` in `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts` (parent WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN).

## Goal
A cheap, cross-process-safe watch over the worklog change signal so the pane can react to an agent write promptly.

## Scope
- `watchDbChanges(cacheDir, worklogDir, opts)`: watches the state-counter file (`state/<hash>.json`) and/or `worklog.db`/`-wal`, debounces/coalesces bursts, and emits a change callback.
- Fail open: any watch/read error is reported as unavailable so the caller falls back to polling. Never throws into the TUI loop.
- `dispose()`/`close()` for teardown on pane exit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `watchDbChanges` watches the cross-process DB-change signal (state counter and/or SQLite `worklog.db`/`-wal`), debounces events, and emits at most one change callback per burst.
- The watch fails open: any read or `fs.watch` error is reported as unavailable and the caller falls back to the 30 s auto-refresh tick.
- Watch teardown (`dispose`) removes all `fs.watch` handles and timers.
- Unit tests cover the watch trigger, debounce/coalescing, and fail-open fallback, with injected `fs.watch`/clock.

## Implementation notes
- Prefer `node:fs` `watch` (no new runtime dependencies). Handle the state-counter file being absent at start-up (watch the `state/` directory or fall back to polling).
- Inject `fs.watch`/timers for deterministic tests (mirror the `db-change.test.ts` mocking style).

## Dependencies
- F1 verification harness (shared contract tests).
data.title: Event-driven DB-change watch primitive

data.description:
Integrate the DB-change watch into the existing gated, single-flight, coalesced refresh path (parent WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN).

## Scope
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`: subscribe to the watch; on a debounced change, request a refresh through the existing `doRefresh` (respecting `inputActive`, visibility, single-flight + trailing coalescing).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`: construct/pass the watcher and worklog dir; teardown on pane exit.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts`: expose an immediate-run/trigger hook without disturbing the tick model, or arm the watch to drive the existing task.

## Acceptance Criteria
- After a work-item write against the shared `.worklog`, the Herdr pane triggers a refresh within 2 s via the event-driven watch, without waiting for the 30 s auto-refresh tick.
- Idle panes still spawn zero `wl` processes per tick; the 30 s tick remains the fallback; a burst of writes coalesces into at most one trailing refresh (no refresh storm).
- Visibility and typing gates are preserved (hidden panes / open text-input overlays skip refresh work); the watcher is torn down on pane exit.
- Integration test asserts the ≤ 2 s trigger and the idle zero-spawn guarantee; coverage extends WL-0MSJ1OLTL009N4IQ and WL-0MTIB7JAN004MQ8N.

## Implementation notes
- Feed the watch into the existing `createGatedTick`/`doRefresh` gate — do NOT bypass single-flight/coalescing.
- Fail open: if the watch is unavailable, polling continues unchanged.

## Dependencies
- F2 watch primitive; F1 verification harness.

implement.py's phase_finish PushNonFastForwardError handler calls run_cmd(['git','rebase','origin/dev'], cwd=cwd) but no 'cwd' variable is defined in that scope (the surrounding code uses repo_root). When dev advances concurrently, the push fails non-fast-forward, the retry path raises NameError, the work item is reset to open, and the already-removed worktree means the committed branch must be pushed manually.

Observed during WL-0MV4VJE8V00478ZF finish (dev advanced concurrently). discovered-from:WL-0MV4VJE8V00478ZF
